public_alpha_issue_ledger.scope: Every open priority:P0, priority:P1, or release blocker issue in the candidate issue snapshot must resolve to one public-alpha classification.

tracked_issues.title: Audit P0: make render route, fallback, and stage failure contracts explicit
tracked_issues.goal: Public alpha must expose one selected route per frame, typed stage results, visible degradation, and first-failure diagnostics for resident, streaming, and serial paths.
evidence_required: PR closes #351 or splits only non-alpha follow-up work with owner and issue link
route/stage failure-injection tests cover resident, streaming, and serial paths
candidate benchmark rows include route_uid, stage_statuses, and fallback_counters for every required lane

tracked_issues.title: Audit P0: close GPU resource leaks and shutdown lifetime hazards
tracked_issues.goal: Public alpha must prove renderer shutdown, compositor shutdown, node removal, and failed initialization do not retain owned GPU resources.
evidence_required: PR closes #352 or splits only non-alpha follow-up work with owner and issue link
GPU/RID accounting tests fail on retained owned resources
candidate GPU harness report includes zero rid_leak_bytes for required batches

tracked_issues.title: Audit P3: define and enforce public alpha release acceptance gates
tracked_issues.goal: Public alpha must be tied to an evidence bundle, issue snapshot, public known-limitations page, and deterministic local contract check.
evidence_required: candidate evidence bundle passes tests/ci/check_renderer_release_gates.py --mode candidate
candidate issue snapshot classifies every open P0, P1, and release-blocker issue

tracked_issues.title: Audit P0: repair opaque qlty check failures blocking renderer PRs
tracked_issues.goal: Do not let opaque external qlty status block the local renderer release gate when GitHub branch protection does not require it.
tracked_issues.rationale: As of 2026-05-21, master branch protection reports required_status_checks=null and the repository tracks no qlty configuration; qlty is therefore an advisory external signal, not a public-alpha release blocker.
evidence_required: GitHub branch protection for master has no required status checks
qlty check is documented as a non-blocking external signal in docs/reference/renderer-release-gates.md and .github/workflows/README.md
candidate issue validation can resolve #369 through this deferred manifest classification

external_status_check_policy.source: GitHub branch protection for master checked on 2026-05-21

non_blocking_checks.reason: The qlty check is not required by master branch protection and has no repo-owned configuration/log contract in this tree.
decision_evidence: repo search found no tracked qlty.toml, .qlty, .codeclimate.yml, or .codefactor.yml policy file
non_blocking_checks.local_gate_behavior: Do not fail tests/ci/check_renderer_release_gates.py solely because qlty check is failing, pending, absent, or inaccessible.

deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.test_name: [TileRenderer][RequiresGPU] Output format coercion keeps deterministic defaults
deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.reason: REPRODUCED 2026-07-19 on b15c6ddda46 (RTX 3090, Vulkan): the TileRenderer batch returns rc=1 with 6/7 cases and 66/67 assertions, failing at test_tile_renderer.cpp:52 -- CHECK(renderer->get_output_format() == RD::DATA_FORMAT_R8G8B8A8_SRGB) reports 232 (DATA_FORMAT_MAX) instead of 42 (SRGB). This is the PRODUCT bug tracked as #643: initialize() returns OK while create_output_textures() (renderer/tile_render_resources.cpp:474) fails to create an SRGB texture carrying TEXTURE_USAGE_STORAGE_BIT, which no driver allows, leaving the renderer with no output texture. The module already has _resolve_storage_compatible_color_format() (renderer/tile_renderer.cpp:104) for exactly this mapping but never calls it on the creation path. || The assertion is CORRECT and encodes the contract #643 must deliver; it must NOT be relaxed to match current behaviour. PR #646 added the [RequiresGPU] tag that routed this known-failing case into the default GPU harness, which is why the gate has been red. Excluding it restores an honest gate WITHOUT weakening the assertion: the case rejoins the batch automatically the moment this waiver is removed. || Origin: unresolved pre-merge review thread on PR #646 (https://github.com/klausi3D/godotGS/pull/646#discussion_r3608341129), which asked for exactly this and was never dispositioned before the admin merge.
deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.mitigation: TileRenderer is not a REQUIRED_BATCH, so no release-gate coverage claim depends on this case. The other 6 cases in the batch (including the sibling shader-compilation case on a real device) still run and still gate. #643 tracks deciding the contract (coerce SRGB->UNORM, or fail initialize()) and then removing this waiver.

deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.reason: REPRODUCED at COMMITTED revision 10198c6141cf3ade8881be767c0bba37b355bd77 (the T4 branch's merge of master 116b45af34e; contains the #908 retag, so the Streaming filter selects the case), RTX 3090, Vulkan, dev binary built from exactly that tree; invocation: bin/godot.windows.editor.dev.x86_64.console.exe --gs-gpu-test --test-case="*GPU Memory Streaming Performance*" -> 1 case, 12 assertions, 2 FAILED at test_gpu_streaming.h:367 (CHECK(ms < 10.0f): 44.72 ms for 10000 splats) and :370 (CHECK(ms < 50.0f): 227.20 ms for 50000 splats). First measured 2026-08-15 on the same case body pre-commit (28.9/33.2 ms vs 10 ms and 144.3/143.7 ms vs 50 ms across two consecutive runs) -- the spread between sessions is itself the point: the budgets were written before the case ever ran anywhere (it was stranded behind the tag-order defect #908 fixed) and were never calibrated against any machine, and wall-clock assertions on this shared self-hosted runner measure the machine, not regressions (#615 measured a 2x swing on a printf-only diff; #630 tracks the contention variance). #910 records the same disposition for the sibling 'GPU Sorting Performance' benchmark: timing cases stay out of gating batches. || The budgets must NOT simply be raised to make the case pass -- that is a threshold edit needing its own justification. Excluding it keeps the Streaming batch's two functional cases running honestly; this case rejoins automatically the moment the waiver is removed.
deferred_requires_gpu_waivers.mitigation: Streaming is not a REQUIRED_BATCH, so no release-gate coverage claim depends on this case. The functional 'GPU Memory Streaming' case (uploads, triple buffering, overflow, invalid parameters) runs and passes in the same batch, so upload CORRECTNESS is exercised; only the wall-clock budget assertions are deferred. #917 is this case's dedicated tracker (deliberately not #892, which closes with T4 -- a waiver blessed by a closed issue is the #520/#329 silent-expiry shape this manifest has already paid for twice); it owns the budget disposition: re-derive calibrated budgets from measured baselines on the CI runner, convert to a relative/telemetry assertion, or retire the case.

documented_non_enforced_rules: manual workflow inputs must not bypass public-alpha readiness
path filters must not downgrade public-alpha readiness
open-world proof must be blocking rather than advisory

workflow_enforced_rules.rule: stable/candidate release publication must not be Linux-only
workflow_enforced_rules.enforced_by: .github/workflows/release_builds.yml release_candidate_gate job (fails the stable/tag path unless both build_linux and build_windows succeeded)
workflow_enforced_rules.checker_scope: The contract checker verifies the release_candidate_gate job marker is present; it does not parse the job's runtime both-platform logic.

workflow_enforced_rules.rule: stable/candidate release publication must not allow unmatched release files
workflow_enforced_rules.enforced_by: .github/workflows/release_builds.yml publish_release sets fail_on_unmatched_files to true when channel == stable
workflow_enforced_rules.checker_scope: The contract checker does not parse the fail_on_unmatched_files value; this remains YAML-level enforcement.

workflow_enforced_rules.rule: a stable/candidate (v*) tag must not publish without passing check_renderer_release_gates.py --mode candidate
workflow_enforced_rules.enforced_by: .github/workflows/release_builds.yml release_candidate_gate job runs --mode candidate on the stable/tag path and fails closed when the evidence bundle is absent; publish_release requires release_candidate_gate success
workflow_enforced_rules.checker_scope: The contract checker verifies the release_candidate_gate job marker is present; it does not parse the job's runtime candidate invocation.
workflow_enforced_rules.remaining_gap: No CI lane yet produces the public-alpha candidate evidence bundle (GPU-harness report, benchmark-lane report, artifact SHA/commit-parity, issue snapshot). Until that pipeline is wired (issue #360), the gate fails closed on every real v* tag; a maintainer supplies the bundle out-of-band via RELEASE_CANDIDATE_EVIDENCE.

workflow_enforced_rules.rule: candidate evidence must be bound to the commit being published and to the exact bytes being shipped
workflow_enforced_rules.enforced_by: .github/workflows/release_builds.yml release_candidate_gate passes --expected-commit ${{ github.sha }} and --artifact-sha <group>=<sha256> for each archive built in the run, requires the Linux BUILD-INFO commit to equal the published commit, and writes release-attestation.json; publish_release re-hashes its downloaded payload with tests/ci/release_attestation.py verify and refuses to publish on any mismatch
workflow_enforced_rules.checker_scope: check_renderer_release_gates.py implements and unit-tests the --expected-commit / --artifact-sha bindings (tests/ci/test_renderer_release_gates.py::CandidateSupplyChainBindingTests); the attestation round-trip is unit-tested in tests/ci/test_release_attestation.py. The contract checker does not parse the workflow YAML that wires these flags.
workflow_enforced_rules.rationale: --mode candidate alone only proves the evidence bundle is internally consistent, so a stale bundle from an older validated commit could authorize publishing newer, never-validated binaries.

benchmark_acceptance.fallback_route_policy: fail unless lane explicitly allows exact fallback route

unbatched_requires_gpu_backlog.note: [RequiresGPU] test cases that match NO named batch in tests/ci/run_gpu_harness.py and therefore execute nowhere. These are NOT waivers: unlike deferred_requires_gpu_waivers (each proven failing, with an owner and an expiry) these cases have simply never been run, so nothing is known about them. Discovered while landing #329, which addressed only the 28 [SceneTree] cases; measuring the whole corpus with correct doctest semantics showed the gap is larger. Recorded explicitly so it is counted and cannot grow silently: tests/ci/test_gpu_harness_deferred_contract.py fails on any orphan NOT listed here, so this list is a ratchet that may only shrink.
unbatched_requires_gpu_backlog.why_not_covered_by_headless_lanes: Every lane in tests/ci/run_module_tests.py:MODULE_TEST_FILTERS carries the exclude '*][RequiresGPU]*', so zero [RequiresGPU] cases execute headless. The one lane that would match them, 'GaussianSplatting [requires-RD]', is catalogue-only, non-strict, runs solely under --run-gpu, and no workflow passes --run-gpu.
